fieldMarks: Largest ground squirrel: 524-1,500 g depending on sex and season
Tawny or cinnamon back flecked with white spots; lighter buff underparts
Tail matches the back at the base and darkens toward the tip
Cylindrical body, short strong forelimbs with sharp claws; cheek pouches
behavior: Diurnal, colonial and territorial; hibernates September to April or May, adults first
Active from about 0400 to 2130 h; inactive in cloudy or rainy weather
Whistle for aerial predators and guttural chatter for ground predators
Eats stems, leaves, seeds, fruit and roots; sometimes lemmings, young hares and bird eggs; stores food in burrow
habitat: Tundra, subalpine brushy meadows, boreal forest and alpine meadows; well-drained sandy sites, often near dunes or eskers; not in permafrost areas.
range: Alaska, Yukon, mainland Northwest Territories and northern British Columbia; ADW gives the west coast of Hudson Bay to western Alaska.
